label: r2c2
name: Conv head + global context
hypothesis: This builds on r1c2's footprint-conv head. It adds a third residual conv with dilation 2 for a wider view, and broadcasts a global pooled vector back into every cell before the head. Placement scores can then depend on the state of the whole build, such as which regions are finished or must be built first. Uses r1c1's longer-horizon recipe; r is about 1.5. Refuted if it scores no better than r1c2 or the starting architecture.
last_analysis: No scores are visible, so I can only compare candidates on priors. All 9 trials trained without errors, and no file ran close to the compute or time limits. Three directions look plausible. (1) Spend the budget on more fresh designs: fewer PPO epochs, gamma 0.99, gae_lambda 0.95. (2) Use footprint-shaped learned convolutions in the action head. (3) Use per-layer heads that reason about the landing layer and the cells a brick seals below it, with a running maximum over lower layers. Global context broadcast (r2c2) was only tested together with a costly dilated conv and the 4-epoch recipe. With one round left, the best use of the trials is to combine parts that each looked sound under the high-sample recipe, and to push that recipe one step further (1 epoch, about 3x the samples). Each trial changes one main thing relative to a trial it can be compared with.
